transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Hart (Redwood AE), Marcus Yoon (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Rajiv Menon (Aurelia ML Platform), Sofia Alvarez (CTO), Evan Chu (SRE), Marta Petrova (Product)

Summary (auto): Agree POC scope: run harness with 3 representative scripts, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, token costs, and streaming behavior. Define success as p95 < 350ms for non-stream, and sustained 200 RPS with 8k token average across sample set (subject to revision after baseline).

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into scope.
[00:12] Rajiv: Hi, Rajiv here — ML infra at Aurelia. We're trying to validate an inference path for our generative insights feature.
[00:18] Sofia: Sofia — CTO. High level: cost + latency balance is the big decision for us.
[00:23] Marcus: Marcus Yoon, SE at Redwood. I'll lead the harness integration.
[00:28] Evan: Evan — SRE. I'll handle the client side load harness and telemetry hooks.
[00:33] Priya: Priya here, I'll help with prompt shaping and evals.
[00:38] Marta: Marta — product, mainly here for success criteria and timelines.

[02:10] Lena: Quick agenda: 1) success criteria, 2) workload sizing and sample scripts, 3) streaming vs non-streaming tests, 4) telemetry, 5) timeline. Does that match?
[02:22] Sofia: Yep, that's what we need. Also want to call out data residency / logs briefly — we'll need audit logs during pilot.

[04:05] Marcus: To start, can you describe your current traffic? QPS peaks, typical token counts, and ratio of short vs long prompts?
[04:18] Rajiv: Sure — right now at prod we see about 120 RPS average across geo, peaks maybe 600 RPS in US-east. But for the feature we're testing, baseline expected is around 50–200 RPS. Token-wise, the mode is ~600 tokens, but we have a long tail up to 6k. 80% of calls are single-turn completions, 20% are multi-turn incremental.
[05:02] Marcus: That's great. For the POC we should pick a mix: short (250 tokens), mid (600 tokens), long (3k-6k) and weight them 50/40/10 to reflect production.
[05:16] Rajiv: Sounds reasonable. We can supply logs to sample exact distributions.

[07:10] Priya: On scripts — we heard you use a prompt templating layer that does dynamic fields and retrieval-augmented bits, any chance you can share sanitized examples?
[07:22] Rajiv: Yes, we have three canonical scripts: first is a short extractive summary, second is multi-step generation with RAG, third is a long-form multi-paragraph explainer. We'll sanitize and send.

[09:05] Marta: Success criteria from product side: p95 latency < 350ms for short and mid scripts in non-streaming mode; for streaming we want first-byte < 120ms with total completion under 700ms typical for short prompts. Cost target is TBD but need a ballpark so we can compare against our current provider.
[09:32] Lena: We'll aim to map cost per 1k tokens and show delta vs current provider. One note — p95 targets depend a lot on batching and cache warmness; we'll define baseline and optimized runs.

[11:00] Evan: On telemetry — we want to emit traces for request lifecycle, token counts, model variant used, and cache-hit metrics. Can Redwood's harness accept OpenTelemetry spans or does it prefer a CSV ingest?
[11:15] Marcus: Harness accepts both. For live runs we can accept OTLP over HTTP and also pull CSV logs. We recommend enabling trace IDs in headers so we can correlate.
[11:30] Evan: Good. We'll wire that up. Also need to know how Redwood reports KV cache warmness — is that per-request metric?
[11:42] Marcus: We can surface a 'kv_cache_hit_ratio' per request in the telemetry. In the hosted sandbox we'll provide dashboards but during the POC we'll share raw metrics too.

[13:20] Sofia: Streaming vs non-streaming: our front-end uses streaming for progressive updates on short prompts; for long prompts we sometimes disable streaming to avoid reflow. We need to see both behaviors.
[13:35] Priya: For streaming tests, we should capture first-byte, byte-throughput, and time-to-last-chunk. Redwood's runtime has some optimizations around chunking — Marcus can you briefly describe?
[13:48] Marcus: Sure — on streaming the runtime flushes tokens based on heuristic batch timeouts and max chunk size. For low-latency streaming we recommend smaller max_chunk_bytes and aggressive flush intervals, but that increases overhead. We'll show tradeoffs.

[15:50] Rajiv: On load harness integration — we use an internal harness that replays production traces. Can we plug our client into Redwood's harness or do we adapt our scripts to Redwood's runner?
[16:05] Marcus: Two options: 1) plug your client via the benchmark harness adapter (we provide a client shim), or 2) convert your scripts into the Redwood harness YAML format. Shim avoids much rework but sometimes obscures fine-grained batching behavior.
[16:24] Rajiv: We prefer the shim for speed, but can convert key scripts if needed.

[18:10] Lena: Timeline proposal: you send artifacts by Sep 6; Redwood runs baseline within 48 hours and shares results; week of Sep 15 start 2-week pilot with weekly syncs. Does that align?
[18:26] Sofia: Yes, but we need SOC2 logs and audit export to be present for the sandbox.
[18:33] Lena: Noted — we'll provide audit logs and an access control matrix.

[20:05] Marta: Clarify success criteria again: apart from latency, the other metric is stability under tail load — p99 should not exceed 1.5s for mid prompts, and error rate should be < 0.1% for the POC.
[20:20] Marcus: We'll include p50/p95/p99 and error breakdown (timeouts, 5xx) in the baseline report.

[22:40] Evan: A question on quantization — we're running some 8-bit quant models in dev. How does Redwood handle quantized model variants and is there a clear performance delta table?
[22:55] Marcus: Yes, we have quant profile recommendations. For Llama-type models you typically see 1.6–2x speedup with 8-bit depending on kernel and sequence length, but memory and quality tradeoffs exist. We'll attach a short matrix to the follow-up.

[25:10] Rajiv: When you run baseline, will you simulate network variability? Our users are global — do you run cross-region latencies?
[25:22] Marcus: Baseline will run in your target region (you told us US-east) but we can add a network emulator to simulate higher latency for specific runs. We can also run across two regions if you want to compare.

[27:30] Priya: On prompt adaptation: some tokens in your templating are dynamic retrieval results — to make harness deterministic we should snapshot retrieval outputs and include them in the sanitized scripts.
[27:45] Rajiv: Yes, we'll provide snapshots for the RAG paths so the harness is repeatable.

[29:05] Lena: Ops question: for the 2-week pilot, what support SLAs do you need — are daily check-ins overkill?
[29:18] Marta: Weekly check-ins suffice; but daily Slack for critical blockers during ramp is fine.

[31:40] Marcus: A few technical clarifications: 1) Do you want streaming and non-streaming runs for each script? 2) Warm cache vs cold cache runs? 3) Do you want sustained 10-minute soak tests?
[31:57] Rajiv: Yes to all. For cold-cache we'll emulate cold starts by flushing the KV store between runs. We'll also ask for a soak of 15 minutes to understand thermal/counter behavior.

[33:20] Evan: Regarding instrumentation — can Redwood emit token-level timing? We want to map where time is spent (scheduling, model kernel, network).
[33:33] Marcus: We emit coarse buckets: queue_time, compute_time, send_time, kv_hit. Token-level is more intrusive and adds overhead; we can do sample tracing for a few requests.

[35:10] Rajiv: For success evaluation, can we see per-prompt cost breakdown so product can compare to our current provider?
[35:20] Lena: Yes — we'll provide token breakdowns and per-call cost estimate for the run. We'll also show optimized runs after we tweak batching and quantization settings.

[37:40] Priya: On metrics retention — what's available in the sandbox? We need 30-day retention for trace logs for compliance during the POC.
[37:51] Marcus: Sandbox has 14-day retention by default, but we can extend to 30 days for the pilot environment. We'll note that in the follow-up.

[40:05] Sofia: A red flag we had with other vendors was mismatch between harness runs and prod because of client-side rate limiting and retries. How does Redwood simulate client behavior?
[40:20] Marcus: The harness can replay production traces including client-side retry patterns. If you provide the traces, we can reproduce retry windows, jitter, throttling. That makes results more realistic.

[42:00] Lena: Ok, recap and owners: Rajiv will sanitize and send three scripts + traffic logs (due Sep 6). Lena to share benchmark template and instructions (due Sep 8). Marcus to run baselines and provide perf/quant matrix (due Sep 9). Evan to enable OTLP headers and test client (due Sep 10). Weekly sync set for Sep 18.

[43:15] Marta: Quick governance note — we'll need a short statement on data handling and retention for our security team, and a contact for SOC2 artifacts.
[43:30] Lena: I'll include the security pack and point of contact in the follow-up.

[45:05] Rajiv: Is there a recommended way to measure cost for streaming vs non-streaming — since streaming may incur more tokens due to chunking?
[45:18] Marcus: We'll provide token accounting per chunk and a normalized cost-per-completion metric that you can compare.

[46:50] Priya: If the baseline misses targets, what's the escalation path? Do we open a dedicated tuning session?
[46:58] Lena: Yes — we'll run an optimization sprint: SE-led tuning on batching, chunking, and model variants; expected improvement within 72 hours.

[48:10] Evan: One small integration detail — our harness uses X-Request-ID for correlation. We'll pass that through; please make sure your logs echo it back.
[48:21] Marcus: Absolutely, we will echo trace IDs and include them in exported CSVs.

[50:00] Sofia: Anything else? If not, thanks — expectation is materials in by Sep 6 and baseline results by Sep 10.
[50:12] Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for Sep 18 weekly and attach the template.
[50:20] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and product terms may be mistranscribed (e.g., kvcache -> 'K V cache', 'Bedrock' sometimes misheard as 'Red rock'). Crosstalk present around timestamps 15:50-16:24 and 31:40-32:10.
